description: Wifi Village at DEF CON 25 covers wireless security, signal intelligence, and RF attacks. The 11 talks explore wardriving, packet sniffing, software-defined radios, home security system vulnerabilities, SIGINT techniques, and wireless monitoring tools like Kismet.

talks.title: WIGLE Like You Mean It  Maximizing Your Wardriving
talks.teaser: Techniques for maximizing wardriving efficiency using WIGLE to map and discover wireless networks.

talks.title: GODUMPiNG packet sniffing the Gotenna
talks.teaser: Packet sniffing and reverse engineering of GoTenna wireless communication devices.

talks.title: Deceptacon: Wireless Deception and Evasion
talks.teaser: Techniques for wireless deception and evasion during penetration tests and red team operations.

talks.title: Designing An Automatic Gain Control
talks.teaser: Hardware design and implementation of automatic gain control circuits for RF receivers.

talks.title: Failsafe: Yet Another SimpliSafe Attack Vector
talks.teaser: Exploitation techniques against SimpliSafe home security systems via wireless attack vectors.

talks.title: Sigint for the rest of us
talks.teaser: Practical signal intelligence techniques and tools for reconnaissance and monitoring of wireless communications.

talks.title: SecureWorks: SDR Replay Attacks On Home Security Systems
talks.teaser: Using software-defined radios to execute replay attacks against home security system sensors and controllers.

talks.title: Hacking Some More of the Wireless World
talks.teaser: Exploration of wireless hacking techniques and tools for discovering and exploiting RF-based systems.

talks.title: Suitcase Repeater Build for UHF 70cm
talks.teaser: DIY construction of a portable repeater system for UHF 70cm amateur radio communications.

talks.title: POCSAG Amateur Pager Network
talks.teaser: Monitoring and understanding POCSAG amateur pager network protocols and communications.

talks.title: Large Scale Wireless Monitoring: KISMET Packet Sniffer
talks.teaser: Large-scale wireless network monitoring and analysis using the KISMET packet sniffer tool.
